payload.friendly_name: Per-PR Sonar reuses CI Modules coverage
payload.purpose_context: On every pull request the SonarCloud reporter re-runs the fast test tier under coverage, costing about thirteen minutes of build time per pull request, even though the per-module test matrix has already produced richer coverage for the same commit. The duplicated run also reports a narrower, understated coverage figure than the matrix does. This mission makes the per-PR report consume the coverage the matrix already produced, so each pull request tests once, reports one consistent coverage number, and returns its result sooner.
payload.purpose_tldr: Stop every pull request from running the fast test tier a second time just to feed the SonarCloud report.

options: Extend sonar.yml with a workflow_run trigger
payload.question: Where should the per-PR SonarCloud scan live once it stops re-running the fast tier?

options: Same-repo PRs only, no fork decoration
payload.question: A Sonar scan must read the PR's source tree, but ci-aggregate.yml deliberately never checks out PR code and would hold SONAR_TOKEN. What posture should the mission take?

options: In scope: mission drives the toggle and verifies live
payload.question: SonarCloud Automatic Analysis is enabled on spec-kitty_spec-kitty and makes every CI-side scan fail with exit 3, independent of this fix. How should the mission handle it?

options: Accept the drop, file a follow-up
payload.question: tests/unit and tests/specify_cli/runtime have no CI home other than the fast-tier step this mission deletes. In scope to give them one?

payload.final_answer: New job in ci-aggregate.yml, needs: collect. Rides the existing workflow_run:[CI Modules] chain and consumes the already-published ci-aggregate-reconciled-coverage + ci-aggregate-source artefacts; inherits that file's workflow_dispatch + mode input so test_dual_mode_contract gates it with no new candidate-tuple entry.

Same-repo PRs only, no fork decoration. Fork PRs get no Sonar today (SONAR_TOKEN is empty on fork pull_request events), so the blast radius stays at today's level and nothing regresses; fork-PR Sonar is a separately-reasoned follow-up, not a side effect of this change.

In scope: add tests/unit and tests/specify_cli/runtime to .github/ci-module-registry.yml so the matrix covers them. Restores their coverage contribution and gives them a real blocking CI home for the first time; the registry stays the single data source for what CI runs.

Separate issue plus a documented prerequisite. File the Automatic Analysis conflict as its own issue and state it in the PR body so a green pipeline is not mistaken for a restored Sonar signal; this mission's acceptance must not depend on a SonarCloud UI action only the operator can take.

options: Restore config from trusted ref after checkout
payload.question: How does the PR source tree reach the scanner without letting the change under review control the analysis?

options: Broaden every row to top-level packages
payload.question: How should the per-module coverage breadth be corrected (FR-013)?

options: Declare it rests on branch protection
payload.question: NFR-003: how is never-merge-blocking enforced in the new home, given ci-aggregate.yml has no verdict job and fleet_verdict.py turns its failures into a red PR verdict?

payload.final_answer: Trusted default-branch checkout stays the working directory (diff-cover depends on it). The validated tested_sha is fetched into a separate subdirectory and referenced via sonar.projectBaseDir/sources; EVERY sonar.* setting is passed as an explicit -D argument resolved from the trusted tree, never read from the PR's sonar-project.properties. Satisfies FR-012 and NFR-008 together.

Broaden every registry row's cov_targets to the top-level packages it can reach. Coverage XMLs merge by union (a line covered in any report wins), so this is correct by construction and needs no per-package mapping to maintain. Accepted cost: coverage.py traces more code per shard, so shard runtime and XML size grow; NFR-002 requires this be measured, not assumed.

Add a terminal verdict job to ci-aggregate.yml mirroring ci-quality.yml's quality-gate pattern, evaluating results and explicitly excluding the Sonar job. This gives the workflow a declarable non-blocking seam analogous to NON_BLOCKING_ALLOWLIST, so SC-006's 'under any outcome' is rule-assertable rather than resting on branch-protection configuration.

Retire the duplicate, execute dispositions, move the documents

reason: Ready for review. RED-first: test_make_target_indirection_resolves_to_a_suite_invocation_live failed with 'assert []' on the current tree (documented blindness, not a typo) before T014; green after. Detection now resolves a run: step's make target by READING the Makefile (variable table + prerequisites + recipe, then the existing pytest parser on expanded lines) -- never by matching the literal 'make test-fast'; a fault-injection twin proves a renamed target ('coverage-tier') behind make variables still resolves, and a negative control proves 'make lint' is still not a suite run. LIVE DUPLICATE IS NOW SEEN, not 'will be once the job moves': load_gates() yields ci-quality.yml::sonarcloud via 'make test-fast' with the real fast-tier paths+marker, selecting 1801 tests, ALL 1801 of which are also selected by >=1 other gate (e.g. ci-modules::test, module-tests::test, ci-router::architectural-heavy). Cascade landed deliberately: WORKFLOW_FILES +3 (ci-quality.yml, ci-router.yml, packs.yml). The latter two were ALREADY running the suite directly but were hidden by a latent parser defect -- 'uv run --frozen pytest' let the --frozen flag's optional argument swallow the 'pytest' command word; also fixed '--deselect <nodeid>' being recorded as a SELECTED path. T016: sonarcloud allowlist entry kept (subject still exists), rationale rewritten -- it no longer claims the derivation cannot see the job, because it now can. T017: no new test file was added (tests live in the two owned modules), so no shard-map edit was needed; note WP04 owns tests/_arch_shard_map.py for registering test_no_duplicate_suite_execution.py. FINDING FOR THE OWNER (I do not own .github/workflows/): packs.yml declares two filter globs that can never fire -- '.claude/**' and '.agents/skills/**' are gitignored in this repo. Recorded in a shrink-only VESTIGIAL_FILTER_GLOBS ledger whose guard reds once packs.yml drops them; deleting them from packs.yml is the real fix. Tests run (targeted, per orchestrator ruling -- full arch suite deferred to CI): test_suite_jobs_gate_blocking.py + test_workflow_coherence.py = 20 passed; 10 _gate_coverage consumers (incl. test_ci_collection_completeness, test_marker_job_completeness, test_same_tier_uniqueness, test_makefile_tier_topology) = 103 passed; 10 shard-map/remaining consumers = 236 passed, 2 skipped. ruff check on changed files exit 0; repo-wide 'ruff format --check .' exit 0 (all three files sit in the shrink-only format-exclude ratchet at HEAD -- reformatting them would break test_ruff_format_exclude_ratchet, so they were deliberately left as-is).

reason: Broadened module-tests.yml so every slice measures the full top-level package set derived from src/ (7 dotted targets, constant across rows); registry + scrub untouched. RED-first evidence (T001 failing on the unchanged tree) and the full cost analysis are in tests/release/coverage_breadth_evidence.md §1. Zero per-file regressions (measured + by construction); +30,226 statements recovered in one slice vs a >=2,808 target. Matrix-union baseline recorded as pending-ci. Finding for WP02: tests/unit, tests/specify_cli/runtime AND tests/architectural/test_no_retired_subsystems.py are in no slice's test dirs - three inputs, not two.

review.reference: APPROVED (debugger-debbie, independent per C-007). Falsification lens: measurements. RED-FIRST REPRODUCED: reverted module-tests.yml to 509b13552c^, ran the gate -> '2 failed, 3 deselected in 0.44s' matching the reported output; restored, current tree '5 passed in 7.10s'. INTEGRATION CHECK REPRODUCED: extracted the COV_PY heredoc, ran it under bash -> exactly 7 flags (charter doctrine glossary kernel mission_runtime runtime specify_cli), byte-identical to the retiring sonarcloud job's 7 --cov flags in ci-quality.yml:190-196, so the 'doctrine' target is REQUIRED not gratuitous (src/doctrine.py is a real non-underscore single-file module; a packages-only derivation would have regressed it). OWNERSHIP: exactly the 4 owned files; .github/ci-module-registry.yml and tests/release/ci_retirement_scrub.json UNTOUCHED (census gate trap avoided). LANE HYGIENE: kitty-specs delta empty, no untracked, no runtime/status files. GATES: ruff check + ruff format --check clean; module-tests.yml parses; targeted blast radius via grep -rl module-tests -> 216 passed in 19.86s (test_coverage_breadth, test_coverage_artefact_contract, test_dual_mode_contract, test_module_shard_registry, test_module_tests_matrix, tests/ci/test_aggregate_attempts, test_aggregate_source, tests/release/test_release_ci_ownership). BASELINE NOT FABRICATED: recomputed from files{} -> 42942/128878 = 33.32%, 1258 files, 998 covered, matching recorded totals exactly. COST ARITHMETIC INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED AND THE ERROR IS CONSERVATIVE, NOT OPTIMISTIC: all stated arithmetic verifies (16.21x34=551s=9.19min; 1352/651.47=2.08; 22.53-19.08=3.45; 12.83-19.08=-6.25). I measured two slices the implementer did NOT: tests/specify_cli/core (narrow --cov=specify_cli) 22.89s->25.56s = +2.65s (+11.6%), and tests/merge (narrow --cov=specify_cli.merge, the maximal fixed-cost case, 18->1236 files) 138.15s->148.97s = +10.82s (+7.8%). Overhead is PROPORTIONAL to slice runtime (7.8-11.6%), not a fixed ~16s/shard, and merge proves the fixed per-shard component is small. Shards are NOT uniform (per-shard test time spans 0.059s-96.8s; 10 of 34 shards under 5s), so 34 x one slice's ABSOLUTE delta is methodologically loose -- but lanes' 11.5% sits at the TOP of the measured range and the x2.08 ratio scales a CPU-bound tracer overhead by a whole-job wall-clock ratio that includes fixed job overhead, while the 22.53min saving removes a whole job and is counted correctly. Both errors inflate the cost side only, so +19.08min is an UPPER BOUND and the -6.25min corner compounds an upper-bound overhead with the single lowest observed saving -- a legitimate sensitivity bound, NOT a likely outcome. The trade is more comfortably net-positive than claimed. NO-REGRESSION: the by-construction argument is sound for WP01's own effect (identical selection; broadening --cov changes recording scope only, so a file's covered set can only grow) and all three of my slices gained files and lost none. ESCALATED TO ORCHESTRATOR, NOT WP01 REWORK: per_file_covered.matrix_union_after is status=pending-ci with files={}, so T004 step 2 / T006 step 1 (diff of TWO baselines) are literally not done; the committed gate never asserts matrix_union_after, so it stays green forever with the stub. WP01 cannot close this (needs CI on a pushed branch; CLAUDE.md assigns whole-suite runs to the CI agent) and the implementer surfaced it precisely in evidence 6. But NFR-009/SC-004 compare retiring-step vs matrix UNION (a different selection), which the construction argument does not cover and which cannot close until the selection gap shuts -- and per task review, no later WP owns (a) filling matrix_union_after, (b) verifying NFR-002 against a real CI run, (c) a registry row for tests/architectural (WP02 adds only two rows; the implementer correctly flags it is three inputs, not two). Three unowned obligations for the orchestrator to place. Pre-existing reds #4365 not attributed here; implementer's one unidentified F from a killed run left unattributed and not counted against this diff.
